extra.message: User-controlled `format` (from the `format` query param) is interpolated directly into a shell command string executed via exec(): `pandoc ${fullPath} -t ${format}`. An attacker who can download a document can inject shell commands (e.g. format=`pdf; cat /etc/passwd`).

User-controlled `localePreset` (from the `charset` query param) is interpolated into `spawn(`iconv -f utf-8 -t ${localePreset}`, { shell: true })`. With `shell: true`, shell metacharacters are interpreted, allowing OS command injection.
`departmentTerm` (from the `department` query param) is concatenated directly into a raw SQL string: `where d.name = '${departmentTerm}'`. This allows SQL injection.

`evaluateCompensationProjectionFormula` builds a function from an attacker-supplied `formula` string using `new Function(...)`. A formula such as `require('child_process').execSync('...')` leads to arbitrary code execution on the server.

`renderOnboardingWelcomeMessage` passes a user-controlled `welcomeLayout` (from the `welcomeLayout` query param) to `lodash.template`, which evaluates embedded JavaScript via `<% %>` interpolations, enabling server-side code execution.

`importDocumentFromSource` fetches an attacker-supplied `sourceUrl` (the `sourceUrl` form field in the document import flow) without validating the host. This permits SSRF against internal network endpoints.

`readPolicyAttachmentFromRecents` joins a `recentPolicyFile` cookie value directly into a filesystem path with no basename/sanitization. An attacker can set the cookie to `../../etc/passwd` to read arbitrary files.
`loadOnboardingChecklistTemplate` builds a path from the user-controlled `templateName` (the `template` query param) without validation, allowing path traversal reads such as `../../app/db/schema`.

`persistChecklistAnnotation` writes a file using a user-controlled `sectionLabel` directly in the path (`path.join(dir, `${sectionLabel}.txt`)`). Traversal characters in `sectionLabel` allow writing files outside the intended directory.

`saveShiftEvidencePhoto` uses the raw `file.name` in `${shiftId}-${file.name}` and writes into the public `shift-evidence` directory with no MIME validation or sanitization. A crafted filename (e.g. `../../...`) or arbitrary content can write files into the public web root.

`applyDisbursementNotice` decodes an unauthenticated, unsigned `notice` and calls `recordDisbursementOutcome`, which can mark a compensation request `effective` and create a compensation record. No signature verification is performed (unlike `applyDisbursementNoticeVerified`), and the callback route has no authentication, so anyone can forge a payout notice.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: `applyScreeningVendorDecision` is an unauthenticated endpoint that trusts a `x-screening-vendor-result` header and applies `{ ...(result as any), updatedAt }` to the onboardingTasks update, allowing arbitrary column overwrite (status, employeeId, reviewerId, etc.) without authentication or signature verification.

`applyProfilePatchFromLink` merges an attacker-supplied JSON `patch` into the employee row via `Object.assign({}, employee, patch, ...)` with no field allowlist. An employee can overwrite arbitrary columns (employmentStatus, managerId, departmentId, title, userId, etc.), escalating privileges or altering employment data.

`assignOnboardingTaskFromForm` spreads all remaining form fields (`...fields`) into the onboardingTasks insert, allowing an HR admin/manager to set arbitrary columns such as `status`, `reviewerId`, and `evidenceDocumentId` that should be constrained by the workflow.

`buildPartnerDirectoryFeed` returns `db.select().from(employees).innerJoin(users, ...)`, selecting every column of both tables including `users.passwordHash` and employee PII (phone, personalEmail, address, emergencyContact). This is returned as JSON by the directory-sync API routes to any API key holder.

`buildPartnerDirectoryFeedForTier` trusts the `x-partner-tier` header to decide whether to attach compensation data (`if (tier == 2)`), without checking the API key's role. A payroll_specialist key (or any allowed role) can set the header to escalate and read salary/bonus data.

This receipt loader fetches any compensation record by id and returns its salary/bonus without calling `assertCanViewCompensation` (the sibling summary route performs this check). Any authenticated user can enumerate record ids and view other employees' compensation.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The shift-summary loader has no authentication; it takes `x-account-id` from a header and returns that employee's shift summary (including derived hourly rate). Any unauthenticated caller can read compensation-derived data for any employee id.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: `resolveClaimedDirectoryScope` lets a manager set a `directoryScope` cookie to any department id and returns the employees of that department, bypassing the direct-report scope. A manager can enumerate employees across departments they do not manage.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The login action redirects to `redirectTo` if it `startsWith("/")`, which also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//evil.com`, enabling an open redirect after login.

`redirectAfterTaskReview` redirects to the session-stored `workspaceReturnTo` value (set from the `returnTo` query param) without validating it is a safe internal path, unlike `redirectAfterRequestReview` which sanitizes it. This enables an open redirect.

`renderMailroomManifestHtml` interpolates `documentTitle` (attacker-controlled document title) into HTML without escaping. A malicious document title leads to stored XSS when the manifest is rendered.
`renderPrintTagScript` places `documentTitle` inside a `<script>` block without escaping. A document title containing `";alert(1);//` breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary JavaScript (XSS).
`buildExportCopyDisposition` interpolates the `document_title` query parameter into the `Content-Disposition` header without stripping CR/LF, allowing HTTP header injection.
`generatePayrollAdjustmentsSummary` catches database errors and returns `error.message` and `error.stack` to the client, disclosing internal implementation details and stack traces.

cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message

extra.message: A hardcoded carrier API bearer token (`cg1_8f42...`) is embedded in `pushEligibilityFileToCarrier` and used to authenticate to an external service.

`buildCompensationProjectionRows` loops `horizonMonths` times with no upper bound. The compensation detail route passes a user-controlled `horizonMonths` query parameter, allowing an attacker to trigger an enormous allocation/loop and exhaust memory/CPU (DoS).

`registerTabletUnlockPin` uses a user-supplied `strengthTier` as the bcrypt cost factor (`rounds = strengthTier || 4`). A client can set a very high cost (e.g. 31) to force expensive hashing and cause CPU-based denial of service.
`applyPartnerFeedCorsHeaders` reflects the request `Origin` verbatim into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and falls back to `*`, allowing any origin to read partner feed API responses.
`recordHrRequestSearchActivity` logs the raw `searchQuery` and `statusFilter` query parameters without sanitizing CR/LF, enabling log injection/forgery.

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs
